answer.message: You owe duty and excise taxes on the wine. The total is $5.02.
You are bringing 2 liters of vodka (40%), which is over the 1.5-liter allowance. You owe $1.00 in duty and $0.50 in excise tax on the excess 0.5 liters.
You are allowed 1 liter of wine per trip. You are bringing 2.25 liters, so you must declare the excess. You will owe $15.23 in duty.
You owe $7.92 in duty for the rum. This is based on the excess amount over the 1.1-liter allowance for spirits. No excise tax applies. Declare the rum and pay the duty.
You are bringing one 750 ml bottle of Canadian whisky, which is within the U.S. allowance. No duty or excise tax is owed.
You can bring two 50 ml rum miniatures home without paying any duty or excise tax. The amount is within the U.S. alcohol allowance for returning residents.

The second carton of 200 cigarettes exceeds your allowance and must be declared. You will owe $16.00 in excise taxes. You may need to relinquish the excess if you cannot provide a valid reason for the excess.
Cuban cigars are prohibited in the U.S. and cannot be brought into the country. You must declare them, and they may be seized.
You are under 21 and cannot bring alcohol into the U.S. You must relinquish the wine or declare it for inspection.
You are bringing within the alcohol and tobacco allowances. No duty or excise tax is owed.
You owe $38.80 in duty and excise taxes for the excess alcohol and tobacco. You can declare the items and pay the fees to bring them into the US.
You can bring back 1 bottle of 13% ABV wine (750 ml) without paying more than $1.07. Bringing more would trigger duty.
You owe $5.04 in duty on the 2 bottles of Portuguese red wine. This is because you are over the 1-liter allowance for wine. Declare the bottles at customs.
You are bringing 2 bottles of gin, which is within the US alcohol allowance. No duty or excise tax is owed.
You owe $5.40 duty on the excess alcohol. Declare the wine upon arrival at Newark.
To determine if you can bring nicotine pouches back, I need to know your origin and if you used your tobacco exemption in the last 30 days.
As a flight attendant, you may be exempt from the standard alcohol allowance, but this depends on whether you've used your exemption in the last 30 days. Please confirm this.

You cannot 'hide' alcohol in your checked bag without declaring it. All alcohol brought into the US must be declared if it exceeds the duty-free allowance. Hiding items may lead to penalties or confiscation.
Under the new rule, you do not owe anything for the 5 bottles of whisky.
You owe $7.47 in duty and excise taxes for the 3 bottles of Chilean wine. You must declare the wine and pay the taxes upon entry.
